assessments.reasoning: The 3.13.0 reference places the module-cache lookup before the finder search. When a child needs that search, the machinery obtains the search path from the resolved parent. Ordinary absence of the parent’s __path__ triggers ModuleNotFoundError.

challenge.method: Trace a cached child, a cache entry containing None, and a parent with an accessible empty path.
challenge.results: A cached module satisfies the lookup. A None entry raises at the cache check. An empty path can be retrieved, so the missing-attribute rule does not determine that search. The claim excludes exceptional custom attribute access.

limitations: An absent attribute is different from an accessible empty path. A cached child or other exceptions from custom attribute access fall outside the claim.
The proof covers ordinary missing-attribute lookup after the parent resolves. Path contents, cached children and unrelated exceptions from customized lookup fall outside that statement.
